title: Stay Calm. Remain Indoors. Dev Diary #7: Reset
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
*"...a law cannot simply be enforced. It must be driven through the skin of the citizen as steel is driven through stone. They must feel the penetration of it; the violation of it. They must understand that the law is not here to reform. That forgiveness lies in another domain. That the criminal to the law is a stain to be bleached out, nothing more.'* 

  
\---

  
After a few days of testing with my tactics game, I have paused and shelved it conceptually. I may return to it, but it just hasn't felt right. 

I want a simulation. 

  
You certainly don't HAVE to use ASCII for a detailed simulation, but it certainly makes an overwhelming job a little easier.

The real curse of ASCII is that while the theatre of the mind it can provide is surprisingly powerful... it is fickle. There's a real fine line to walk in this type of game between how much the player watches vs how much they interact with. 

  
My initial thoughts for this experiment are that the player will watch a world-building sequence, a bit like legends mode in Dwarf Fortress but much more zoomed-in, that will lead to the same fundamental place every game but with a lot of variation. 

Then the player builds a character, and they play that one character directly while playing in a sandbox where you have a lot of indirect influence and can tip the scales in a lot of ways and watch how things unfold. 

At the moment, I kind-of think it'll be a bit immersive-sim-ish, maybe a bit Mount & Blade (or that's the north star, anyway).
